items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: the lead, Jack Kapp had a cigar store Indian out there, right there for the bands

ctx.x: you could get the sound, you could get four saxophones, you could get five saxophones, and you could hear them. Before you had to have pretty much, you know, three saxophones or two saxophones and the same way with the brass. You got heavy brass and bands begin to have a larger sound, a larger scope, besides they would have flutes and they would also have the lower register of the saxophone, and the machines would take the recording.

I can remember recording up at Decca when you couldn't do that. I would have something like that in the arrangements. and they would suppress it. Tighten it up. Bring a vocalist in, all the time, that. I would ask one of the guys, "Can't you give me more body?" "No, all you want to hear is the vocal anyway, is what we want." the lead, Jack Kapp had a cigar store Indian out there, right there for the bands -- he can't hear -- he doesn't understand the jazz, give me the melody, and that's true.
